name: Modern 3-Level 4BR/4BA Mission Home | Deck +Garage
description: This three story, 3,000 square foot, modern Mission District home has an open floor plan perfect for entertaining, and four bedrooms, four full bathrooms, a private sun-drenched roof deck, and an enclosed back yard. It's located in close walking distance to the 24th Street, Mission Street, and Valencia Street corridors, and also has garage parking and is easily accessible by car and public transit from all points in the Bay Area.
host_about:
A San Francisco native (my first day care was just five blocks from where I am now), I lived in San Diego for college and New York City for graduate school.  After working big corporate jobs in New York for five years, and then in San Francisco for three after moving back, I decided to try to go out on my own, and build a small business and consulting practice.

To help with income as I got started, I decided to rent two spare bedrooms in my home.  But even as my business has grown, I've found that the enjoyment and excitement of hosting travelers from around the world -- in a house that I love, and in the neighborhood that continues to awe me -- has been something I've wanted to continue.  For it brings me great pleasure to open up my house to visitors and share with them all that I marvel at in SF.

A foodie, and an outdoor enthusiast, I'd be delighted to share with you my favorite restaurants and hiking spots (and as a volunteer guide at Muir Woods, I could regale you with redwood facts for an hour), or to assist with your trip planning in any other way that I can.  

I hope that I can help you have a perfect trip, and that you get to enjoy Casa de Virgil, the Mission District, and San Francisco as much as I do!

host_about:
AnneKarin was born in Chicago to Henry P. and Elly Glass.  Theirs was an artistic household.  Henry was educated in the Wiener Werkstadt and was one of the founders of the field of Industrial Design in the U.S.  Elly was a member of the Viennese Dressmakers’ Guild.  Both of them taught at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.  AnneKarin grew up in Northfield IL and graduated from New Trier HS in 1961.  She received her BA in Anthropology from the University of Illinois, Urbana, in 1966 and joined the Peace Corps that same year.  She served as a Volunteer for three years in Ilheus, Bahia, Brazil, where she founded a leather working factory that provided steady work for local shoe makers.  Upon her return she went to Illinois Institute of Technology where she received an MA in Linguistics.
She tolerated the weather in Chicago until 1973 when she moved to San Francisco where Peace Corps friends facilitated her settlement into a new life on the West Coast.  Two months after she arrived she broke her leg in a ski accident and spent 11 months in a cast.  When able to walk again, she pursued a sign painting business which grew into a brokerage for architectural graphics.  From that she moved into print brokering, specializing in 3-D displays.  This enabled her to buy the house she was living in on Potrero Hill in San Francisco.
The recession in 1989 plus the introduction of computer technology into the world of print created a crossroad.  AnneKarin decided to give up the printing business and return to graduate school where she earned a graduate certificate in Educational Therapy.  She specialized in perception/cognition and opened a private practice, helping children and adults with learning disabilities to address the underlying causes of their learning problems.  
During all these years AnneKarin continued to pursue visual art.  Today she works as an artist, focusing on the figure.  When no model is available she enjoys painting still lifes, abstracts, and landscapes.  She has shown her work internationally and in many competitions across the U.S.  She is a member of the Artists’ Guild of San Francisco.
AnneKarin lives with Clebia, whom she met in Ilheus when she was a Peace Corps volunteer. Clebia is a case worker for intellectually challenged adults and a gourmet cook.  Clebia and AnneKarin enjoy travel, walking in the outdoors, fine dining, music, the ballet, who done-its, and old and new friendships.

We have been working on this space for the last 2 years to get the details just right, including hand built furniture and art by local artists.  Above the din of the Mission, this apartment is a unique space built in the attic of a large Edwardian house run by artists Laurel Roth Hope and Andy Diaz Hope .
host_about:
I'm a sculptor who lives part time in San Francisco and part time in the redwood forest 60 miles outside of SF. For traveling, I lived in India for 8 months, and have done some traveling in England, Germany, the Netherlands, the US, Costa Rica, and Venice, and always hope to do more. I usually travel with my husband (who I sometimes collaborate with on artwork) and now our young daughter as well.

After several years of renting our apartment through AirBnB when we were out of town, we spent over 2 years building a beautiful and unique 2 bedroom guest suite with private entrance, bathroom, and kitchenette in our light filled attic. We're proud of the space and enjoy hosting guests there.

I'm pretty quiet and love animals, parks, reading, movies, and walking in new places.

host_about: My wife and I have lived in San Francisco for 40 years; prior to this, we lived in the Los Angeles area for nearly 10 years. I am originally from Hungary. I left when I was 16 in 1956. We have traveled extensively in Europe and South America and welcome international and national guests.  We love living in San Francisco and taking full advantage of the geographic, social and cultural activities it has to offer. Our home is I a perfect location to easily explore the city and its intriguing, diverse neighborhoods. host_about:
We may be new to AirBnB but we have been renting our San Francisco home to guests for over 15 years and have rented many places away from home for our travels over the years. We are careful and considerate non-smoking guests who take good care of the places we stay and are looking for guests to stay in our home who will do the same. 

We have over 200 5 star reviews on our other platforms (VR/HA/TA) so you can rent with confidence that you will have a great place to stay aided by thoughtful, helpful and experienced hosts.

We are a retirement age couple who find ourselves away from San Francisco often these days. Although we love our home and we love San Francisco, we also like to travel. Now we rent our home to guests like you while we are away. When we are home we are usually working to upgrade and refresh our house. We know you will enjoy the results!

We have lived in the San Francisco area for almost 50 years and purchased our San Francisco home in 1999. In 2004 we began to spend time away and a friend suggested we offer it to guests on vacation or in San Francisco on business. We soon learned that people really enjoyed our home-like atmosphere. We are thrilled with the response we have gotten and we work hard to keep our new and returning guests contented and feeling cared for. Visitors say they appreciate our clean and well appointed home and our knowledge of the city and professional attitude.

Most guests mention the feeling of a being in a real home as soon as they enter. We think this is because we still live there part of each year and keep the house comfortable and well maintained not only for our guests but for ourselves as well. We are also proud of our garden, keeping it maintained even while we are away. We paint, scrape, clean, renew, update and replace parts of the house every time we come to visit. We think it shows. 

Our guests certainly enjoy our home. Read the reviews! 170 Five Star ratings on HA/VR and 75 on TA. We get these ratings not because everything is always perfect (we do try, however!) but because we go out of our way to help our guests settle in and feel at home and we respond quickly to any question. Finally, if you are bringing a car, you will absolutely love our little garage (for economy to mid-size cars). Parking rules in SF can make you dizzy. If you don't bring a car - great! - hop on the bus one block from the front door and head downtown or to the beach.

You can read more about our home at YourHomeInSanFrancisco. 
Thanks!

name: Cozy, private suite with separate entrance.
description: Private, cozy suite with a bedroom, living room, kitchen area, and bathroom. We have just about everything you need to make this your home away from home in our wonderful city.
host_about:
We are a family of four doing the best we can to stay in this breathtaking, but increasingly expensive city. Ken has lived here almost all his life. Chloe has lived here half of her life. Gemma and Freya, the most charming girls ever, were both born here and will hopefully make San Francisco their home when they grow up.

Ken is a government employee, and Chloe works for a labor organization. Gemma is a five-year old who is currently attending preschool -- she's heading to kindergarten August 2020. Freya is a three-year old who has recently begun attending Gemma's same preschool -- she heads to kindergarten August 2021.

We began using Airbnb back in 2013. We can't stop saying good things about the platform, which enabled us to travel to far away locales for reasonable prices and explore as the locals would.

We know the City probably as well as (and likely better than) any native. Ken's lived here for almost 40 years. In our free time, we enjoy visiting parks, cooking and exploring new restaurants. 

In opening our home to the world, we are obviously looking to earn some extra money to enable us to stay in San Francisco. But that's not our only motivation, as there are many other ways to make money. One of the reasons is to enable Gemma and Freya to potentially be exposed to people from different parts of the world and to teach them the value of experiencing the world through travel when they grow up. And in welcoming people regardless of color or creed, we hope to instill in Gemma and Freya our city's famous philosophy to live and let live. Gemma and Freya are always fond of meeting you, if you give them the opportunity!

The Bayview is an exciting neighborhood that is currently in flux. New residents (like us) are slowly changing the makeup of the neighborhood, but longtime residents seem to mostly take it all in stride. Come to the Bayview to explore our magical city. We can't wait to meet you.

name: Stylish Modern Getaway, Biz Friendly
description: Looking for a convenient and quiet place to stay while exploring San Francisco? This is it! The space is located on a busy street, but the bedrooms are quiet, comfortable, stylishly decorated and homey. It’s close to public transportation, making it easy to travel anywhere in the City. host_about:
I enjoy traveling and experiencing the local life in new cities. I like to pack my day with as many activities as possible on some trips, while I want to relax more and take my time on others. Either way, I love spending time roaming around, finding the popular touristy landmarks I can not miss and seeking out the little gems that would otherwise be hidden. It's always helpful to get a locals' perspective, and that's why I enjoy opening up our home to host those who visit the Bay Area! We like to give our guests an experience that we would appreciate if we were traveling. That way, we're always doing our best to be helpful, understanding, and accommodating. 

When I travel with my wife, we don't usually spend much time in the places we rent because we're usually out and about... all we need is a clean place to shower and sleep. We know not all travelers are like us, and that's why we take extra care to make the home feel cozy and welcoming for our guests! We like presenting a clean and comfortable space to our guests with the basic necessities so all they have to do is arrive and enjoy! 

Our guests' experiences staying in our home are important to us! We believe they will be amazing if both the guests and the hosts mutually put in effort to respect each other and contribute to a positive environment. Just as we aim to provide a space that we'd like to travel and stay in, we similarly treat others the way we would want to be treated. Our guests' feedback usually tell us we are accommodating and quick responders, doing our best to provide a great experience for them. We are grateful for their kind words, but what's important is that we can deliver the same great experience to you! We are Julia + Frank, two European expats calling San Francisco home for 28+ years, sharing our longtime home when traveling.

We have a passion for art/architecture/design and a penchant for food/travels - and we love to explore the world along roads less traveled.

Our work life frequently takes us to far away places, often on unpredictable travel schedules, so we cherish returning to the sanctuary of our home - appreciating house guests who share our values + treat our home with utmost care.

host_about:
I live in a beautifully, newly decorated home by the Pacific Ocean.  I love the ocean.  The  fresh, crisp air that it brings rejuvenates me.  The ocean also reminds me of the far off lands I have visited, and the friends I have made when doing so.  Europe (Germany, Spain, Italy, Turkey), Mexico, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, and of course, where I am from, China, are just some of the places I have traveled.

China holds my fondest memories, not  because I was born there, but because China is where I learned all about cosmetology and the holistic healing arts.  I was a successful, award winning Cosmetologist in China, and moved to the United States to seek even greater opportunities. Today, I own several successful businesses, and help thousands of people achieve the beauty they desire.  However, what I really enjoy, is in sharing the richness of our cultural diversity with others...that is what makes America great. Our country has the ability to weave many diverse cultures  into a beautiful fabric that unifies all of us.  I truly look forward to sharing with others, and making their stay the most memorable experience possible.

description: Welcome to my clean and beautiful modern home within the Excelsior District of San Francisco!  Located near Mission and Geneva, it's right next to the city's best taquerias. host_about:
Hi, I'm Doug! As a native of San Francisco, I attended SF's Lowell High School and graduated from UC Berkeley with a degree in Molecular Cell Biology and a minor in German.  I'm a huge Bay Area sports fan, and I try to go to the gym at least twice a week!

During college, while studying abroad in Germany for a year, I took the opportunity to fly and to rail to 10 of the neighboring European countries.  I've also spent some time traveling solo in South East Asia.  I really enjoy immersing myself in different cultures as I find the challenge especially rewarding.  I can understand and speak a little German still.  My Mandarin is embarrassingly poor.

name: SF Home- Mins to the Beach, 20 Mins to Downtown SF
description: Sunny and Spacious 2 bedroom home in the Sunset  that's perfect for those coming to explore or work in SF! Walkable to both Ocean Beach and SF Zoo while only being a 10 min drive to Golden Gate Park, and a 20 min drive to either the Golden Gate Bridge or Downtown SF!
host_about:
Greetings from Noelle and George!

We both grew up in the Bay Area and are college sweethearts having both majored in biological sciences. We chose to live and raise a family which includes our three children in San Francisco because of the beautiful landscape, amazing culture and diversity, priceless climate and lets not forget exploring this beautiful city through the iconic cable car rides.

As a family we enjoy spending most of our time outdoors which includes hiking in the Marin Headlands, breezy walks along Ocean Beach, as well as biking in Golden Gate Park to name a few. Camping is a major part of our summer routine in Lake Tahoe, Yosemite National Park, and Camp Mendocino. We also enjoy Lake Tahoe during the winter months for skiing and snowboarding. Noelle and I are also avid sports fans and LOVE attending San Francisco Giants, Oakland Athletics, Golden State Warriors, San Francisco Forty Niners, Oakland Raiders and San Jose Shark games with our children and friends. Our weekends are also consumed with youth sports as our children play on baseball, basketball, golf, and swimming teams.

 We are lucky enough to live in an area which embraces the arts and we are just a short stroll away from the many music festivals which San Francisco has to offer and a few of our favorite events to attend are the Blue Grass Festival and Outside Lands both in Golden Gate Park. 

San Francisco offers a variety of multi-cultural cuisine all within a short distance from each other whether it be a walk, drive or door step away. Some of our favorites include, fresh seafood, Pho, Mission-style burritos, Korean BBQ, Cioppino, or exploring our palates with tasting world renowned wine and cheese at the Ferry Building!

name: The Mission Room in 1906 SF Victorian
description:
"The Mission Room" is a PRIVATE (not shared) cozy & comfy room in a restored classic SF 1906 Victorian flat.
It is meticulously cleaned and disinfected in between guests; door knobs & all. In addition, the house common areas are cleaned 3 times a week & hand wipes are in every room.
Free Organic Coffee, Tea & Mexican Hot Chocolate.
Strong WiFi
Free Washer/Dryer w soap.
Close to groceries, boutiques & restaurants.
2 Blocks from 24th BART, Public Transportation & Freeways.
host_about:
Hola! 
I love to travel, the last place I went was the Caribbean in Honduras (awesome) &  I have been day dreaming about my next destination-Colombia.  I also love to dance-all kinds but Samba is my religion!
For an authentically Mission experience there is a free Salsa lesson included in your stay- I can teach you in 15 mins -yes  it's that easy or well,  just enough to fake the rest...
I also love gardening, culture, fashion, camping, history and living in SF.
For 23 years, I owned one of the last Latin cultural stores in the community, it was a landmark legacy business which gave me a very intimate & spiritual connection to the Mission- hence why I  was  picked to film an Airbnb success story commercial you may have seen on u-tube called 
"Airbnb Nancy" - what a blast! 
 I love showing guests the best of SF life, here are some of the best things to do beyond the touristy sights: 
-Bike along the embarcadero, across the GG bridge & take the ferry back from Sausalito- epic! 
bring some Napa or Sonoma Chardonnay with you &  on the  way stop at a crab stand at Fisherman's Wharf to pick up a very affordable crab sandwich on sourdough for the Quintessential San Francisco meal- have a picnic at Aquatic Park or Chrissy Field. 
-Hike Lands End 
-People watch at Dolores Park - best sunset view is at 20th & Church-don’t miss the irreverent Hunky Jesus (look a like) contest on Easter Sunday 
-Catch some blues at The Saloon in North Beach Sunday night 
-Eat a burrito in the Mission, Best in the US & do a self guided mural walk thru Balmy Alley & around. 
-Eat Dim Sum in Chinatown 
at the Hang ah Tea House & stop by The Fortune Cookie Factory nearby, (invented by a Japanese man)
- Eat buffalo stew or burger at historical Tommy’s Joint & be transported back to the days of the Barbary Coast 
-ok The Cheese Cake Factory above Macy's Union Square can be a bit new money & a little touristy, but the food is actually pretty good & the view is AMAZING
-The museum on the 2nd story of the Boudin Bakery in Fishermans Wharf is a little gem & you can see how the bread is being made into turtles, dolphons, crabs & other adorable animals.  After that head to Musee Mecanique a few doors away for antique arcade machines, relics left from Playland that used to be at Ocean Beach.
-Play "I left my Heart in San Francisco" by Tony Bennett & read some Herb Caen, who coined the term "Baghdad by the Bay" 
-Have some coffee at Caffe Trieste in North Beach, where  the 1st Capuccino in the West was served  & also where Francis Ford Coppola wrote The God Father.
- See the Zapatista Mural in Jack Kerouc Alley, painted by a dear friend &  behind iconic City Lights Bookstore .  Ask me about the mural story.
-Catch a baseball game at Oracle park !
SF songs & bands : 
City Lights by Journey
The Grateful Dead of course
Huey Lewis & the News 
Carlos Santana  & more !

You can also see the guide I made for Airbnb's  Mission Institutions:
https://www.airbnb.com/things-to-do/insider-guidebook/108?location=San%20Francisco%2C%20CA%2C%20United%20States&source=&currentTab=place_tab

...p.s. once you know Salsa you also know Cumbia, Merengue, Bachata...

host_about:
It is just me and my husband here. I have lived in San Francisco since 2006. I graduated from SFSU and love the City. I have mostly done non-profit work so it's been a great hub for me. We can't live without an ocean near by and I love the smell of the sea in the air. We feel fortunate to live in a neighborhood with art, cafes, boutiques, grocery stores and sushi (a few doors down). 

The place itself is a classic SF flat, it's not modern at all but it's a very colorful place that is reminiscent of a time in the city where every house was a big beautiful Victorian. The house is as colorful as the neighborhood is. The Mission is covered in murals and gorgeous paintings that tell stories.

There's one word that fully encompasses the experience of staying at our hostel: Community. Our adventure travel company launched in 1974 with the purpose of bringing together folks who share the same single ambition: Travel! For the next twenty years, our buses brought these wandering souls to experience places as close as Santa Barbara and Monterey, to destinations as far as Alaska, New York City, and even Costa Rica. As incredible as these destinations are, we believe it is more about the journey than the destination.  

In the 1990’s we opened our San Francisco hostel to offer a haven for travelers to settle, rest, and of course party! In opening our hostel, we hoped to create a sense of community and create a haven where these newly found friendships would flourish.  We believe that bringing people together to create a community is the true purpose of a hostel.

Community. That’s what we’re about.  Stop by and experience it for yourself.

description:

host_about:
I was born in Panama, Central America, and raised in Chile, South America! I'm a nature and animal lover who absolutely enjoys traveling and exploring this amazing world full of cultures and mind-blowing landscapes :D

While I was living in Chile, I went to Veterinary Medicine school, where I graduated as a Dr. for Large, Wild, and Endangered animals. If you were wondering, yes... I don’t eat meat  : )

When I moved to SF, my life had a big turn, and I started a new path where I got trained as a Birth and Postpartum Doula, Childbirth Educator, Midwife Assistant, Pre & Post Natal Yoga Instructor, Reiki I, II & III Practitioner, Certified Massage Therapist with the main focus on women’s health, Certified Pre & Post Natal Yoga Teacher and currently going to school for Homebirth midwifery <3.

name: Gorgeous Garden Apt near Golden Gate Park
description: This bright and beautiful garden apartment is walking distance to Golden Gate Park, beaches, restaurants, museums, hiking trails, and more. We love our neighborhood, and so will you! Fully equipped kitchen, spa-like shower, very comfortable. French doors open to private deck with bubbling fountain and lovely garden. Private entrance via keypad. Several close bus lines take you directly downtown. All on one level; wheel-chair friendly.  Click our profile pic to read our 90+ excellent reviews!
host_about: Hi!  We are Tim and Lisa.  These are a few of our favorite things: Our adopted city of San Francisco (we've both lived here over 3 decades), our local neighborhood (the Richmond District), meeting people, nature (birds/beaches/hiking/etc.), live music (especially at SF's fantastic music venues, including the music festivals right here in Golden Gate Park), food, and our family (we have 2 adult daughters and 2 grandkids).  We met while teaching at the well-respected preschool that Tim co-founded in 1984.  Tim comes from a hotel/restaurant family (The Treadway Inns in New England), and now newly retired, he looks forward to returning to his family roots as a friendly and helpful host.  Tim loves to garden and cook. Lisa still happily teaches 2-, 3- and 4-year-olds (coming up on her 31st year at the same school).  Like Tim, she is also from the East Coast (NY).  We put tons of love, care, comfort and quality into building our new apartment, as we expect to live down there ourselves one day.  We currently live upstairs from the apartment and are therefore easy to contact if you need anything (our guests choose how much or little interaction to have with us).  Please let us know if you have any questions!

host_about: The Story of the "Sea of Love" began when Rajvi's Dream became a reality.  Having always wanted to own a second home in Southern California where two of her young adult children are attending USC (she is a Trojan too) and Rajvi has many clients, she set out to transform a run down Spanish style duplex into a beautifully restored pristine architectural gem to be shared with family and friends - new and old - from near and from far.  Growing up in West Covina, it was only apropos that this gem happened to be located on Covina Avenue.  If that wasn't enough coincidence, the property was built the year Rajvi's late mother was born. Simply stated, it was meant to be! Teaming up with brilliant Canadian born and San Francisco based architect Ian Murray and locally loved and amazingly talented general contractor Don Robinson, Rajvi set out on a renovation path that lasted nearly nine months.  Partnering with her husband Gurinder and  experienced SuperHost Susan Bailey (a UCLA Bruin nonetheless) to manage the property - Rajvi is now perfectly positioned to share her "Sea of Love" with guests from all around the world.  It is with immense gratitude that we share our love of the ocean, our home and Belmont Shore with you!

host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

Excellent, spacious house on a cul-de-sac. Three bedrooms, two baths. One bedroom on the entry level with en-suite compact bathroom, shower. Window with lovely treetop and city views.
Main attraction is the top floor. Living-dining rooms with sliding glass doors out to a deck, yielding majestic cityscape and bay views. Two big bedrooms with big closets. One with queen bed, second with two twin beds. Full sized bathroom in hallway. Cook-in kitchen with gas stove. Big garage. Glen Park area.
host_about:
'Not all who wander are lost.' I love this quote. 
I am that wanderer, incredibly lucky to be infected with the passion and audacity to travel often and solo. 
I was born and raised in San Francisco. I am a native. I love my city. I’ve watched it evolve. But I have also left it many times in my youth. I’ve left it to study abroad in France. Best decision of my college life! I backpacked solo around western Europe. 
I’ve left SF when I was in the military and stationed around our country. I’ve also driven as far north as Niagara Falls.
Career wise, I’ve spent over a decade in property management and rentals. I'm also a realtor. As a hobby, I write as often as possible, a pen and notebook on me at all times.
I am cursed with this blessing of being unceasingly interested in people. I love meeting people. I love hearing stories. And I love writing them. 
As I review my life’s experiences, I’ve come upon one very simple realization, that proclaimed secret of success. It is merely this: ‘Say what you will do and do what you will say.’
The prolific Seth Godin, talented blogger said creativity isn’t the most important part. What counts is being able to ship! Ship on time. And ship again. And again. And again.

name: "Designer  Showplace  Home"  in the Marina
description: Beautiful Mediterranean sunny bright cosy spacious elegant 3 bedrooms, 2 baths apartment in charming quaint Marina District. Located 1 block from the Palace of Fine Arts, St.Francis Yacht Club, beach & 5 blocks to Chestnut Street buzzing with restaurants, bars, boutiques, cafes/bakeries, banks etc. 5 minutes walk to great hiking trails. Walking distance to: Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Point, Fort Mason, Presidio Park, Disney Museum, Union & Polk Streets, Fisherman's Wharf, China town, Union Square.
host_about:
I am from the Mediterranean area and have been an artist all my life . I am an interior designer and a real estate agent working with Keller Williams. 
I am professional, hospitable, very quiet, non smoker, extremely clean, open minded, athletic, social, interested in the arts, real estate and business.
I love nature and outdoor activities. I snow ski, swim, hike, bike, dance, cook, draw and paint. I enjoy watching movies such as: Like Water for Chocolate, Chocolat, Les Intouchables, Gladiator, Braveheart, The Lion King, ET, Avatar, Pretty Woman, Shawshanck Redemption, The last of the Mohicans, Pride & Prejudice, the history channels, documentaries, etc... 
I am sociable, outgoing, hospitable, love good conversation and great food. I traveled extensively around the world and lived abroad. Since my teens, I try each year, to discover one or 2 new cities or countries. I enjoy learning and discovering new cultures as I appreciate people and the world.
Some of the main countries I have visited in Europe, South America, Central and North America including the Arab World are:
 France, England, Italy, Germany, Austria, Sweden , Denmark, Portugal, Spain, Basque, Greece, Cypress, Turkey,  Lebanon, Jordan, Syria, United Arab Emirates, Israel, Morocco and the Sahara desert.

name: Home in the Heart of the Mission
description: Welcome! Our centrally located home is perfect for couples and families. Walking distance to close to 100 restaurants, shops, Alamo Cinema Draft House, farmer's market, bars, live music, parks, public transportation and a block and a half from BART… Sunny, warmest neighborhood in SF, culturally diverse, bursting with life. High Speed Internet, HD TV, Direct TV, HBO/Showtime.  STR-0005118
host_about:
My wife and I have traveled the world, but have called San Francisco home for 25 years. We invite you to stay with us in our 1896 Edwardian home in the middle of the Mission District, San Francisco's oldest and arguably most vibrant neighborhood filled with a diverse range of some of the City's best restaurants, bars, parks, shops, and more. Not to mention our neighborhood is the warmest, flattest, and fog free part of San Francisco. 

We're 15 minutes from SFO by taxi, a block and a half from the 24th Bart Station and close to many bus and MUNI (subway) lines. Having visited Southeast Asia, Oceania, Australia, Europe, Central America, and of course all over North America, one theme holds true for all our adventures: discover the true culture and flavor wherever we are. 

As your host, we'll do everything we can to make sure you get off the beaten path. We're happy to share our favorite restaurants, local hangouts, and ensure you see the true San Francisco, not just the typical touristy sites. We're into everything from scuba diving, biking, kayaking, hiking, wine, art, music, food, festivals, museums, all things teens, parks, and more. Whatever you're into, we'll point you in the right direction so you have an authentic and memorable time in San Francisco. My motto is from the great Mahatma Ghandi: "Be the change you wish to see in the world." Our style of hosting reflects the needs of our guests. When possible, we like to meet our guests. However we understand that many of them are busy on a tight schedule or not interested to meet us so we respect that. We want to make sure every guest is comfortable and part of that is respecting boundaries and their personal space. 

We look forward to hosting you soon! If you have any questions, please feel free to ask. We're just a click away.

host_about:
I moved from my native country of Japan to the Russian Hill neighborhood of San Francisco over 20 years ago and I plan to stay here forever. I truly love San Francisco and Russian Hill in particular. I manage my own art business and love collecting and restoring antiques. I also love traveling, wine tasting, hiking, visiting museums and galleries, cooking, and checking out new San Francisco restaurants and coffee shops.

I am passionate about respecting and maintaining San Francisco’s old world charm. I personally restored this property, keeping as much of the original details that I could while creating a comfortable atmosphere with modern conveniences. I want guests to have an authentic San Francisco experience, and hope the space I have created will make you feel at home. 

Because I have lived here for so long, I can provide guests with tips on sites and local restaurants that are off of the beaten path. I can also recommend neighborhood walks that expose guests to the historic and cultural charm that San Francisco has to offer. Since I often go to Napa and Sonoma, I have many recommendations of wineries that you may want to visit. 

I am proud of my adopted city and my home and want to share them with you. I hope that you can experience all the wonders of San Francisco that I am so lucky to enjoy everyday.

If you like my property, please add it to your Wish List!

host_about:
My Motto; "Every Day is a Good Day!"

*As of February 27, 2022  I was fully vaccinated by way of the Pfizer all available vaccine and the two boosters available. I also contracted Covid 19 or a variant in May 2022 and fully recovered.

Something about me and my home; I’m gay, 64, single, very fit and energetic, very outgoing and easy going. I have always lived in California and have traveled the world extensively. I absolutely love San Francisco and even more being in the Mission District. Entrepreneurial spirited, at age twenty-one I started a business which fulfilled insurers’ responsibilities for auto losses involving vandalism and retired from that adventure just shy of 36 years later.  I have been vegan for four years now and I have redirected my culinary skills towards all things plant, sugar-free, and fat-free based cuisine.  I enjoy practicing yoga at Love Story just around the corner.  I am also an avid bicyclist and use my bike as my primary mode of transport in the city.  I am attending  Community College SF working my way to a zoological degree. Life is good.

As for my home, the location and views are arguably the best the Mission District can offer. The private roof deck, a green oasis for the otherwise concrete jungle of a Mission Street residence. My place faces west so it's on the street side and is usually quite noisy from people, traffic and sirens. Thankfully the residence was constructed in 2008 and  built  quite soundproof. The bedrooms are well sized and comfortably appointed. The sun always seems to shine in the Mission District.

Finally, I love being an AirBnB host which allows me to share my good fortune, meet wonderful people and make new friends. 

I hope that you choose to stay. 

Mark

name: Artful Comforts in the Lower Haight
description:
I am rethinking my post COVID listing. Hopefully, the situation will be clearer.
I am fully vaccinated.
As a result of Covid, I thought about lowering my price. I have concluded that I am charging a very fair price for my home. If you like art, paintings and photographs, my home is the place to stay. If you live nearby and you want to stay two nights, I will make an exception. Thanks for considering my home. I have had two vaccines and three boosters
host_about:
I live  alone in my our art filled home in the Lower Haight — central to everything. I retired from working downtown in Union Square; it takes very little effort to get there, three stops on MUNI. Our public-transit system is everywhere and very close to the house (be it a MUNI, the N Judah — underground — or the street car on Market Street). Our closest surrounding neighborhoods are Hayes Valley, Duboce Triangle, The Castro (just underwent extensive renovations), the Upper Haight and Valencia Street in the Mission District. On Waller Street we're literally steps away from some of the best food, bars and shopping (not tourist spots). The Lower Haight was voted the number one neighborhood in San Francisco by the tech community. Most important, do not rent a large car or let the car agency upgrade you to a larger car. Parking is too difficult. The rental agency tries to unload larger cars by offering visitors an upgrade. Don't accept it. I allow my guests to park in the street in front of my garage providing there is enough room.

My home (pre earthquake Edwardian) has been with me for more than forty years, so you can ask me anything that you want to know about the Bay Area and I am  bound to point you in the right direction. What else... Ah, just feel free to be in touch. I look forward to having you around! I just concluded my ninth year as a host on Airbnb. I am continually told that my price is too low. I am OK with my fee. I really want my guests to have a great time when staying in my home. To paraphrase the clothing designer Tom Ford, " Surrounding yourself with beautiful objects, enhances the quality of your life". It is my  unofficial motto. 

After hosting many guests from many different places, I learned that it is important to understand that when you book my home you are also experiencing my life. I have friends that stop by. I occasionally have people for dinner. It is essential to understand that I am not a professional innkeeper. I am not running a bed and breakfast. I am an Airbnb host who accept guests to stay in my guest bedrooms. I want my guests to live like residents of San Francisco. My neighborhood is very popular. When you stay with me you are returning to your San Francisco home.

name: Peaceful Noe Home with Office and Patio by 24th Street
description:
Welcome to a quiet oasis in Noe!

Noe Valley Luxury Modern is both a family and business traveler friendly space located in a fully rebuilt house that turned a single family cottage from the 1880's into a contemporary multi-level home built for this millennium's lifestyle. High-end finishes and amenities throughout, wonderful indoor-outdoor living spaces, and virtually everything you could possibly need within 2-5 blocks. Think urban boutique hotel - but with a LOT more space!
host_about:
Andy is a life-long traveler, thrilled to finally be back home in the Bay Area where he grew up and where his extended family still resides.  In 2008 Andy and his wife Tanya were fortunate to find a classic Noe Valley fixer-upper and moved into the cute, tiny Pioneer Victorian where they lived for almost 6 years.  In 2013 they began a complete reconstruction of the 1880's cottage and in 2014 moved their family back into a completely transformed contemporary house equipped for this millenium's lifestyle - the Victorian front remains, but everything behind it now meets the needs and expectations of today (hello, closets and gigabit ethernet...).  Andy has been an at-home Dad since 2000, and has worked in tourism, academia, and as a professional chef.  He loves the vibrant food culture in San Francisco and only wishes he had more time to take advantage of all the amazing arts that San Francisco dishes up on a daily basis as well as the wonderful outdoor spaces, hikes, and bike rides that are nearby.  Andy is very knowledgeable about San Francisco food and fun and is happy to make suggestions to help your stay be enjoyable, fun and tasty, whether you are here for business or family pleasure.

Andy has enjoyed a wide variety of travel styles and accommodations over the years, from $3/night huts on beaches in Eastern Indonesia, simple Ryokan in Japan, and luxury hotels and chateaux in the US, Asia and Europe: the apartment is equipped to closely match the experience of a boutique hotel - luxury finishes throughout and thoughtful amenities - but with a lot more space than most boutique hotels provide!

description:
*Minimum 30-day rental
*Nightly rate includes Airbnb service fee and cleaning fee

Our suite has recently been refurbished with a bathroom remodel, fresh paint, new TV and many other upgrades. We've organized it to be private, secure and comfortable. We aim to create an atmosphere that is enjoyable and restful.
host_about:
We're proud of our excellent ratings, so please take a moment to read our reviews! We strive to make your stay with us a five-star experience.

We have lived in our home for over 25 years and every day we feel fortunate that we live in beautiful San Francisco.  Our children were raised in our great neighborhood, the Inner Sunset district, and many of our neighbors are longtime friends. We're excited to share the wonders of the city to all who visit our SF Suite.

Both of us are career media professionals who have joyfully  transitioned to working in community arts organizations.  

We have visited many places in the U.S. and abroad  and our many travel experiences have given us great insight in how to host. We have always enjoyed staying in private spaces to get a feel for how the locals live. On our travels we have enjoyed cooking our own meals as well as eating out. Hopefully our guests will benefit from what we've learned along the way about hospitality and comfort. 

Our hosting style is service-oriented but not intrusive, where your privacy and comfort is our priority. We live on the premises, above the suite and are always available to help our guests have the best stay possible.  We look forward to meeting you!

~Syl and Art

description:
This is a thoroughly sanitized private room(s) that opens to the courtyard in our 1886 Victorian. The rooms have a permitted private kitchenette and great amentities. There is a modern bathroom (shared with 1 other guest at most). There is an optional second room available. Inquire w/ us.

host_about:
Greetings!

My name is Warren C. Lathe III, I go by Trey (a nickname, means "3" :). I am a career biologist (molecular genetics) though currently, I'm writing, teaching and other things (like Airbnb!). 

My partner in crime since 1996, and legal husband since 2008, is Guy and we have two school-age (middle and high schools) children (the picture here was 8 years ago :D). Guy is an English as a Second Language teacher by training and career, but now manages properties.

We have a long and deep connection to San Francisco. Guy is a Berryessa. The Berryessa's settled San Francisco and the bay in the 1770s coming with the De Anza party in 1776. His GGrandfather was Jose de los Santos Berryessa.  Guy's parents were married and lived in this city during the '40s (while his father fought in the Pacific theater). My own parents moved to the Bay Area in the 80's. Guy and I both moved into this home in 1997. San Francisco had been our dream city for its acceptance, tolerance, family heritage and its beauty. It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

host_about:
Seb and I have been hosting guests on Airbnb since 2010. We have a 3 year old baby.  I work as a psychologist with kids and spend weekends working in my garden, cooking, relaxing around the neighborhood. I have lived in the Mission for last 18 years and love talking about the neighborhood, world travels and good places to eat. The house tends to be pretty quiet and mellow. We specifically do not rent to couples so that there are a max of three guests at any time.
Sebouh lives downstairs and you will see him occasionally. He speaks fluent Armenian and is a plumber and works out of our house, so he comes and goes throughout the day.

name: Luxurious, modern, beautiful A+view
description: It's an amazing deal, one of the best in SF, especially for those traveling for a short or extended time. You will fall in love with my historic Pacific Heights home and the unbelievable view. You will enjoy the large, open space and all the upgrades
host_about:
I am a physician and I moved to USA 22 years ago. I love what San Francisco city and the Bay Area has to offer. I feel very lucky and privileged to live in a beautiful and safe area of San Francisco called Pacific Heights. 

I am an avid mountaineer/climber and I travel usually once a year, for a month - long expedition trip. That is usually when I open the calendar in AirBnB for my apartment, as well as (separately) for my garage. 

I would like to rent my beautiful home to someone reliable for all that time when I am gone. 

The things I can't live without are my family, friends, mountains, my amazing home, nature, meditation and any kind of physical activity daily. 

My favorite travel destinations - to many to mention. I feel amazing in high altitude mountains. 

I climbed all the highest mountains in the world called Seven Summits (including Mt.Everest), as well as skied to the South Pole.  Beside that, all my travels and expeditions left me with amazing memories. 

My favorite books - too many to list here as I  read a lot, but I love the most  "Master and Margarita" by Michail Bulhakov. There are many books in my home, so if you have time feel free to read something new. I switched now to ebooks or audiobooks, as it doesn't take any physical space. 

My favorite food is prepared with local and organic ingredients - check out many restaurants on Fillmore street - you will have so many to choose from, even after Pandemic years. I love sushi and the best sushi in the city is a walking distance from my home - check out Tataki restaurant (on California street/Divisadero street) - amazing and fresh! 
I also would encourage you to check “State Bird Provisions”, but you would need a reservation. It’s a 7 -10 minutes walking distance from my home. Located on Fillmore street. 

I travel a lot for business - Marriott hotels, but for fun - I prefer staying in a tent or in a cool Airbnb place in different cities all over the world. 

My motto in life is to live largely, “on the edge of my comfort zone", hence climbing or polar expeditions, and now posting my home at Airbnb website. 

Throughout the process of renting my home I learn that my HOA’s CC&Rs (Homeowners Rules) do not allow for any short term rentals and I can only rent it for a month or longer. 

My modern apartment is located on the top floor of the beautiful Victorian (freshly painted) building (originally from 1896). I have the best view of Japan Town and Twin Towers as well as complete privacy in my home. 

I love green plants and I have many in my home and at the balcony. I’ll be very grateful if you could please water it once a week ( just a little bit :) to keep it lush and green. 

So far, I had wonderful guests from all over the world for the last ten years. I am super grateful for all people I met through AirBnB. 

Please feel free to ask me any questions before you send a reservation. 

I look forward to meeting you in person and to host you in my home.
 
Thank you.

name: View of Mission Dolores Church in a garden setting
description:
This studio has gets lots of light in the morning and is peaceful with the view of Mission Dolores Church in the background. It’s about 280 square feet. You can’t beat the location and privacy. You also have direct access to a common shared garden. It’s a perfect place to come home to after working in the city or exploring. The location is the best. You don’t need a car when you stay here.
VERY IMPORTANT! Before you book, please read my pet and parking disclosures statement below.
host_about:
Hari Om, I’m born and raised in San Francisco.  I’ve lived here all my life except for 4 years in Thailand.  I’ve been vegan for  5 years and completely sober for 10 years.  I’m always looking into any way I can improve myself.   My favorites are meditation and yoga.   My interests are bike ridding and staying in shape.  

Today I’m self employed by working for neighbors as a Handyman but my main purpose  is taking care of my 88 year old mother who lives with me.  I moved her into the garden cottage that’s on the property 3 years ago.  I recently bought her a multipoo dog  to keep her company.  You might run into Dandy during your stay here.   
I really like hosting people via Air b n b and I believe I found my calling being a “super host”.  I try my best to treat people like family here.  I normally feel my guests vibration and can tell how much they would like to engage with me.   Sometimes people like to be left alone and I get that. I respect people’s privacy.  Most of my guests like to be friendly and I’m ready to answer any questions or concerns that they might have.  My goal is to provide an excellent experience to all my guests.  


Roberto
